utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: This is a Status Conference to look at the state of affairs regarding witnesses. Since we've been unable to continue for the rest of the morning and we are not sure whether we shall have the witness on Wednesday, the Trial Chamber wanted to find out from the Prosecution if they can bring a witness for Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I note that the accused are not present, but it's not necessary for them to be present.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. I spoke with Ewa Tabeau, and she would be available. It's Wednesday afternoon, if I'm correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Gentlemen. From Wednesday it's afternoon until the end of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He yes. She would be available for this Wednesday, if necessary. If Mr. Todorovic is unable to testify, we could put Ewa Tabeau on. If they're prepared -- because it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are always cooperative with our friends and with the Trial Chamber with regard to the proceedings and stuff like that. In this particular matter, I would like to tell you: Yes, we know that Ms. Ewa Tabeau will come as an expert witness. We've been working on that topic since. But Your Honours, we are in big problem. For example, I myself, I'm in the middle of preparation of the cross-examination of Mr. Todorovic, who is quite important witness, especially for my client. It would be rather difficult now to shift or to wait whether we shall have him or Ms. Tabeau. Another matter which is important: We Defence counsel, prior to these hearings, we, in the last couple of weeks, we divided our portions of possible cross-examination of Ms. Ewa Tabeau. Thirdly, Mr. Pisarevic is away. He is a part of the team of Defence counsel who will give certain cross. He will be back on I believe Monday. Mr. Lukic is leaving tomorrow. Only I am here. And for this really specific reasons, we are in problem how to rearrange, how to organise our cross for Ms. Ewa Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, but it has always been a rule in the Tribunal that Defence counsel must always be prepared for the Prosecution case. This is not the first time that we have to change witnesses because of certain circumstances that have arisen, that has happened before.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I absolutely agree, Your Honour, but this is a specific situation. You can understand my position with this witness testifying against my client. This is a really important witness as well as for Prosecution. And also, Ms. Ewa Tabeau is also of great importance for the, of course, Prosecution and us. So it's unfortunate event that these two particular witnesses are now overlapping, so to say, and we have to work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm afraid that has to be the case. We shall just have to overlap. Because we just can't wait for the other witness when we don't know when his pain will be dealt with by the dentist. We will have another witness on Wednesday. Tomorrow we aren't sitting because we haven't got a courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If you permit me, Your Honour, if maybe our learned friend can maybe arrange a videolink with the other witness or maybe someone who is nearby, maybe Ms. Kapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's not possible, because the Trial Chamber did look at all those possibilities. It's not possible. Because we don't want also to interrupt the closed session for too long because of the fact that the witness is a serving prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I might have somewhat of an alternative. It might be helpful to everybody involved. Ms. Tabeau, as you know, within her statement has all sorts of charts. I could put her on the witness stand, have her -- show the charts here, have her demonstrate the basis of each of the charts, basically bring her through a limited direct examination which would probably last an hour, hour and a half, which would take up some of the day, a good part of the afternoon and if they would want to cross-examine her next week, I'd have no objection, if that would make it easier for them and have their attorneys back that have to do that cross-examination. If that would -- if that's what the Court wants. But I could be ready at least to take part of the afternoon. Also, we're filing some motions on video conferencing, as well as protective orders, so there are other matters that we will be filing today which the Court could take up at least a good part of the day on Wednesday. If that's what the Court wants. I'm filing -- I'll give you some background. I'm filing protective orders on three witnesses today which two have been -- actually, all three have been interviewed will be 92 bis witnesses, as well as a video conferencing for Mr. Hasan Subasic. Hasan Subasic is the witness that is living in Salt Lake City Utah, within the United States. Mr. Subasic was supposed to be here and testify just before this witness who is on now, either that or just after this witness. Mr. Subasic was involved in a car accident within the month, has a broken collarbone, broken arm, broke ribs. It would be practically impossible for him in that condition to travel, so we'll be filing a motion based on that to do videolinking within the United States, probably through the federal district court in -- wherever it is within Utah. So we have to view that motion. Whatever the Court would like, we're here to help. If there's going to be a problem on cross and you need something, we can do the motions, administrative matters, and I will put her on for direct examination, go through her charts and do whatever is necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm really grateful to my learned friend. Thank you very much. That would be really -- help us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. You are agreeable to what Mr. Weiner suggested. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. I'm really much a obliged to the words of my learned friend, really. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And we'll get the motions that we're filing today. They will all be in the Defence counsel room at the end of the day, so they will have a chance to study them and be prepared to answer in court on Wednesday to the government's or the Prosecution's motions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. So we'll have that witness, Ms. Ewa Tabeau, on Wednesday. We are starting our proceedings at 1415. In the event that the continuing witness is not well enough to continue. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just as an aside, Your Honour, is there any information from the Registry as to a dental appointment or have we learned any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber has been informed that everything is being done to get an appointment as quickly as possible, yes, so that he can be attended to.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, then. We shall adjourn until Wednesday at --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As there are no other subjects, colleague Pantelic already informed me, and the Registry informed me. I have another 20 minutes concerning my cross-examination, and I hoped to conclude it today. However, this unforeseeable circumstance concerning the health of the witness occurred. And I talked to Mr. Tadic. We agreed that Mr. Krgovic would then carry on the next 20 minutes, although the registrar already mentioned that I would have these 20 minutes which Mr. Krgovic will then carry on. And I wanted to confirm, in connection with Madam Ewa Tabeau, we have divided the various areas we will be covering in our cross. I have also some talks with our investigators. Therefore, I'm grateful to the Prosecution for this proposal of theirs how to organise with the expert witness Ewa Tabeau and then from Monday onwards we'll be present here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Co-counsel can always continue and complete the cross-examination when the witness is well enough to continue. So we'll adjourn until Wednesday at 1415 hours.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
